status_rationale: Gate C is benchmark-auto approved (reviews/ptx-or-b16/benchmark-auto/ptx-9.3-or.b16-ab7bd730-c-benchmark-auto-v1.json). Lean mapping v2 exists in namespace Spec2Lean.PTX.OrB16 with no outstanding mapping defects. No proofs are written at this stage.

unit.bounded_unit: PTX ISA 9.3 bounded scalar form `or.b16 d, a, b;`
unit.scope_boundary: Only .b16 with optional predicate predication and register-file + predicate-file state is in scope. Source2 immediate is not modeled in this bounded Lean artifact; destination `_` is not asserted by the mapping.

compliance_notes: No proofs are included at this stage.
No vacuous function-totality/determinism claims: relational determinism is over OrB16Step, with explicit function/relation bridge obligation handled separately.

Open-question- and design-dependent parts are respected: this set does not assert bit-bucket semantics for destination `_` nor immediate support for source-b beyond what is represented by SourceB.reg.

validation_obligations.title: Bounded instruction syntax and operand order
validation_obligations.description: Instruction structure includes optional guard and exactly fields (d, a, b) for destination then two sources, with .b16 type and no additional operand constructors in the mapped artifact.

validation_obligations.title: 16-bit bounded value representation
validation_obligations.description: B16 is represented via `Fin (2^16)`, enforcing bounded 16-bit values in type and ensuring all state writes remain within 16-bit domain.

validation_obligations.title: Minimal state + partial outcome convention
validation_obligations.description: MachineState contains only value-register and predicate maps; `execOrB16` yields `Option` outcomes and returns `none` for malformed guard/predicate or unresolved source reads, preserving the partial-execution convention.

theorem_obligations.intent: For fixed pre-state and instruction, `OrB16Step` has at most one post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For all states s and instruction i and states s1 s2, if `OrB16Step s i s1` and `OrB16Step s i s2`, then `s1 = s2`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB16Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : OrB16Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : OrB16Step s i s1) (h2 : OrB16Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both `executed` and `notExecuted` branches are possible in the relation via guard and read-resolution behavior; the theorem excludes the possibility of two distinct relation outcomes from one fixed `(s, i)`.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case-split on h1 and h2. Branch mismatch on `evalGuard` values is impossible; same-constructor cases simplify to equality of update expressions and reflexive state.

theorem_obligations.intent: Relate `execOrB16` outcomes to relation steps in both directions and characterize partiality with `none`.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) if `execOrB16` returns an executed state, then that state satisfies `OrB16Step`; (b) if it returns notExecuted state, then that state satisfies `OrB16Step`; (c) if `OrB16Step s i s'` holds, then `execOrB16 s i` is some executed/notExecuted outcome matching `s'`; (d) `execOrB16 s i = none` iff no relation step from `(s, i)` exists.
hypotheses: h : execOrB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')
h : execOrB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.notExecuted s')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Four-way correspondence between function and relation including partial-completeness.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The function includes three observably different outcomes (executed, notExecuted, none); correspondence must match constructor-level branches and is not a reflexive property.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold `execOrB16` and `OrB16Step`; split on guard and source lookups for soundness/completeness, and use existential packaging for part (c).

theorem_obligations.intent: Under true guard and resolved sources, executed post-state writes register destination with `orValue va vb` at the selected destination.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If `evalGuard` is true, destination register is `r`, and sources evaluate to `va` and `vb`, then `execOrB16` returns executed state `s'` with `s'.valueRegs r = some (orValue va vb)`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem execOrB16_or_result (s : MachineState) (i : OrB16Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B16) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) (ha : evalSourceA s i.a = some va) (hb : evalSourceB s i.b = some vb) : ∃ s', execOrB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (orValue va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : evalSourceA s i.a = some va
hb : evalSourceB s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: executed state writes `orValue va vb` to the destination register.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: This explicitly pins the concrete computed value written by the instruction (`a | b`) to the resulting state, rather than only asserting some write occurred.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Use hguard and source hypotheses to force executed branch, then simplify updateDestination with hd and evaluate by definition.

theorem_obligations.intent: A false-guard instruction step preserves the full machine state unchanged.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If `OrB16Step s i s'` and `evalGuard s i.guard = some false`, then `s' = s`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB16Step_false_guard_preserves_state (s : MachineState) (i : OrB16Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB16Step s i s') (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) : s' = s
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The theorem proves a meaningful effect of false-guard predication in relation semantics; it is not implied by mere totality of a function.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold OrB16Step and resolve constructor mismatch from hguard; only notExecuted constructor remains, yielding reflexive state equality.

theorem_obligations.intent: Predicate register file is unchanged by the relation step; only value register destination may change in executed case.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any step `OrB16Step s i s'`, for all predicates p, `s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB16Step_predicate_file_frame (s : MachineState) (i : OrB16Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB16Step s i s') : ∀ p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The bounded state model includes predicate lookups, so invariance is a meaningful locality claim for this execution relation.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Both constructors of OrB16Step update only `valueRegs` (executed) or leave state unchanged (notExecuted), so `predRegs` is syntactically unchanged in either case.
